**Summary of findings and decision:**

1. **Fleet data shows sustained May rebound (doy 140-152)** at 0.2-0.67 yt/angler, not the dead zone I predicted. Water temp at 19°C supports El Niño baseline.

2. **My October-only strategy was based on Season 2 (La Niña calendar)**. Season 6 is El Niño with data-driven peaks, not calendar-driven.

3. **New plan: Adaptive probing instead of holding dry.** Book one THREE_QUARTER trip this weekend (doy 154-155) for $150 to test if rebound sustains. This low-cost probe preserves $250 + 10 PTO for follow-up or October fallback.

4. **Gap to leaders is 9 fish.** If October peak fires + May probing works, I can reach 17-20 total fish and rank 3-8. If I keep holding dry, October no-show leaves me stuck at rank 10.

**Updated notes document the pivot from calendar-locked strategy to responsive, data-driven approach.** Next decision point is doy 162 (after first probe results), where I'll decide on second booking based on whether fleet sustains >0.4 yt/angler.

I've captured the core insights in my private notes; next step is the booking decision at tomorrow's briefing.
